q: The Talagrand inequality T₂(C) states that for a probability measure μ satisfying it, every measure ν satisfies:
opts: W₂(ν,μ)² ≤ C·D(ν||μ) (Wasserstein-2 distance controlled by KL divergence)
exp: Talagrand T₂: W₂(ν,μ)² ≤ 2C·D(ν||μ). The Gaussian measure satisfies T₂(1) (Otto-Villani, 2000). Talagrand T₂ is implied by the log-Sobolev inequality (LSI with constant C) and implies the Poincaré inequality. This chain LSI → T₂ → Poincaré encodes increasing concentration.
